'''Alexander Haas''' (born 1964 in [[Heilbronn]]) is a German [[biologist]] and has been a professor at the [[University of Hamburg]] since 2003.<ref name="Welt">{{cite web |url=https://www.welt.de/regionales/hamburg/article2444244/Von-der-Faszination-der-Froesche.html |title=Herpetologie: Von der Faszination der Frösche |last=Schütte |first=Gisela |work=[[Die Welt]] |date=14 September 2008 |language=de}}</ref><ref name="Zeit">{{cite web |url=https://www.zeit.de/2009/08/N-Biodiversitaet-Interview |title=Tierbestandsaufnahme: Gern gelobt, ungern gefördert |work=[[Die Zeit]] |date=2009 |language=de}}</ref>

Haas heads the [[herpetology]] section at the [https://leibniz-lib.de/en/index.html Leibniz Institute for the Analysis of Biodiversity Change]. Before his appointment in Hamburg, he studied at the [[University of Tübingen]], spent a year at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in California, and spent nine years at the [[Friedrich Schiller University Jena]].<ref name="Welt"/><ref name="Zeit"/>

Together with his colleague Professor [[Indraneil Das]] of [[Malaysia]], Haas has conducted an inventory of frog species and [[tadpole]]s in the Malaysian states of [[Sarawak]] and [[Sabah]] on the island of [[Borneo]] since 2004. The research project, ''Inventory and Biodiversity of the Frog Fauna of East Malaysia with emphasis on their larval forms'', was supported by the [[Volkswagen Foundation]].<ref name="Welt"/><ref name="FrogsBorneo">{{cite web |url=https://www.frogsofborneo.org/ |title=Frogs of Borneo |work=Project website of Alexander Haas and Indraneil Das |language=en}}</ref>

In the context of [[biodiversity]] conservation, Haas advocates foundational work in [[taxonomy]], arguing that such work is necessary for the rapid documentation of biodiversity.<ref name="Zeit"/><ref name="Welt"/>
